info.name: Total Expert Public API
info.description:
The Total Expert REST API allows you to programmatically create, retrieve, update, and delete information through various endpoints.

Documentation Layout

Each section of this documentation describes a collection of related endpoints that affect a given resource.

Where applicable, at the top of a section you will find a table listing the attributes for the resource and a second showing its relationships with other resources.

NOTE: If an attribute is marked as 'Assignable', its value can be set via a POST/PATCH. You can also modify the data for an 'Assignable' relationship.

Authentication in the TE API

Interaction with the TE API is protected with OAuth 2.0. A client ID/secret pair is required to use the API.

The ID/secret pair is used to request an access token from the '/token' endpoint. This token will need to be present within the header on all calls to the API.

NOTE: See the 'Authentication' endpoint collection for more information. See the 'Heartbeats' endpoint collection for more information on how to test your authentication.

Endpoint Standards

Each endpoint provides interaction with two aspects of an entity:

'Attributes' - Attributes of the entity itself. Includes things like first name, phone number, or birthday of the contact.
E.g. A 'Contact'

'Relationships' - Describe a relationship between that entity and another entity.
E.g. A contact that has an owner in the TE System OR a set of contact groups (separate entities with their own endpoint).

Attributes

Each endpoint returns a JSON object with a set of attributes. Each endpoint collection should describe the names and types of attributes available in each endpoint.

Data Types

Each attribute has a type. There are four data types in the TE API - Numeric, String, Boolean, and Date.

Data Types
Type Description
Numeric Integer or floating point numbers. Supplied with no surrounding quotes. e.g. { "loan_rate":4.5 }
String String of characters - supplied surrounded with quotes. e.g. { "first_name":"Clark" }
Boolean Truth value - supplied in one of two ways - see Boolean (String) and Boolean (Numeric) for details
Boolean (String) Truth value - supplied as the word "True" or "False", surrounded by quotes. e.g. { "first_time_buyer":"True" }
Boolean (Numeric) Truth value - supplied as the number 1 or 0, not surrounded by quotes. e.g. { "first_time_buyer":0 }
Date A date and time - preferred supplied in the format "YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm:ss". All dates must be provided in UTC timezone. When returned, the value will be expressed in UTC. To clear a field with a date type, use the value "0000-00-00 00:00:00".
Phone Numbers

Phone numbers are accepted in any format. For deduplication, any non-numeric symbols will be stripped out and the numeric phone number will be stored separately. If a numerically identical phone number is used in a different format later, the records are compared using the numeric value only. This applies only to phone numbers with at least 7 digits.

All phone numbers will also be converted into E164 for use in external services (e.g. Twilio). If a phone number cannot be converted into E164, the number will be marked 'Invalid', and external services that rely on phone numbers will not function.

Uniqueness in the TE API

Each type of entity in the TE API can be uniquely identified by a set of attributes. In some cases, multiple options are available to uniquely identify an entity. See each section below for details. These sets of attributes are used to deduplicate entries on creation and to uniquely identify the target in a relationship.

Relationships

Relationships in the TE API are very flexible.

'GET'ing

When GETing an entity, a relationship will be returned with only a partial set of attributes that make sense in the context of that endpoint - e.g. the 'contact_groups' relationship on the '/contacts' endpoint will display only the group name of the target contact_group.

POST and PATCH Requests

When setting a relationship (by POST or PATCH), the target entity is specified using one or more attributes that uniquely identify the entity.

The allowed attributes are listed in the 'Settable Fields' column of each Relationships table. For example, when POSTing to the '/contact-groups' endpoint, either of the following are allowed:

  • {
    "group_name": "Hot Leads",
    "owner":{"username": "alfred"}
    }
    OR

  • {
    "group_name": "Hot Leads",
    "owner":{"id": "123589"}
    }

In cases where an endpoint's relationship supports multiple Settable Fields be aware that the request examples may only make use of one of the attributes though any could be used in its place.

Interacting with the API

Admin Calls vs User Calls

You'll notice that many sections of the documentation have samples for POSTs and GETs that are labeled "As Admin" or "As User".
When using client credentials to access the API, you'll use the "As Admin" examples. For Authorization Code access, you'll use the "As User" examples.

'GET'ing

There are two types of GETable endpoints in the TE API: Paging and Individual. Paging endpoints provide lists of entities. E.g. '/contacts' returns a list of contacts.

Getting Individual Entities

Individual endpoints return specific individual entities, specified by TE ID. E.g. '/contacts/51151' returns the contact with the 'id' attribute '51151' (the TE internal identifier).

Getting Multiple Entities (Paging)

Paging endpoints will return an object with two properties: 'objects' and 'links'. The 'objects' property will be an array of entities in 'pages'. Each page will have a number of entities along with a set of links. The page size and page number can be specified using the '?page' GET parameter. Setting '?page[number]=5' will return the fifth page. Setting '?page[size]=100' will make each page consist of 100 items, instead of the default of 10. Both attributes can be set together. E.g. setting '?page[size]=100&page[number]=6' will return items 501-600.

Paging Links

The 'links' attribute on a page object will have four attributes, specifying metadata about the number of entities available to page.

  • 'first' will be the page number of the first page of entities (always '1').

  • 'last' will be the page number of the last page of entities.

  • 'next' will be the page number of the next page after the currently requested one. 'next' may be null if there are no subsequent pages.

  • 'prev' will be the page number of the page immediately preceding the current one. 'prev' may be null if there are no preceding pages.

'POST'ing

Entities can be created in the TE system by POSTing to paging endpoints. E.g. sending a POST to '/contacts' will create a contact.

Deduplication

When POSTing an entity, the TE API will attempt to 'Deduplicate' by searching for existing entities with similar attributes. If such a duplicate does exist, the TE API will treat the POST as a PATCH to that entity instead. See each section for details on what attributes will be used to search for duplicates.

'PATCH'ing

Entities can be updated in the TE system by PATCHing to individual endpoints. E.g. sending a PATCH to '/contacts/51151' will update the attributes of the contact with TE 'id' of '51151'.

'DELETE'ing

Entities can be deleted only by TE ID. Send a DELETE request to the appropriate individual entity endpoint to delete it.

Return Codes

Where applicable, the API will respond with an HTTP status code that indicates what happened during the request. Possible values include:

HTTP CODES
Status Code General Description
200 SUCCESS The operation completed successfully. See the response body for details (if applicable).
201 CREATED The object was created successfully. See the response body for details (if applicable).
400 BAD REQUEST The JSON supplied to the API was malformed and unparseable.
401 UNAUTHORIZED The request's credentials are invalid. This could mean your token has expired and should be renewed. See the response body for details.
403 FORBIDDEN An attempt was made to access a resource for which you do not have permission
405 METHOD NOT ALLOWED An attempt was made to interact with an endpoint in an unsupported manner, e.g. sending a POST to '/contacts/1'
415 UNSUPPORTED MEDIA TYPE The API endpoints expect a content type of 'media/json'
422 UNPROCESSABLE ENTITY The JSON body supplied is valid, but not processable semantically. For example, the 'owner' relationship for a contact refers to a User that does not exist in the TE system.
418 I'M A TEAPOT The API is a teapot (See the 'Heartbeat' section for details).
503 SERVICE UNAVAILABLE The API is unavailable. Please try your request again later. If this message persists, please contact Technical Support

item.name: Authentication
Fetch a Token From Client Credentials Grant

request.description:
Supply client credentials to obtain an access token.

If you are integrating with the Total Expert API from a confidential client you will likely want to use this endpoint. For the client_credentials authorization grant type you will need to make certain that your client is also the resource owner.

Authorization Header Encoding

Shown in the HEADERS table below, the Authorization header field implements the Basic Authentication Schema. The 'basic_auth' value needs to be a base64-encoded string containing your client_id and client_secret. The string that you encode must be in the format:

yourclientid:yourclientsecret

The following are examples of methods that can be used to base64-encode a string.

On BSD/Linux/Mac run:

echo -n 'yourclientid:yourclientsecret' | openssl base64

(note - this often injects one or more newlines into the encoded string, remove it before using to authenticate)

For Windows see:

https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/kb/191239

Using The Token

To interact with the secure endpoints in the TE API, supply the token in the 'Authorization' header as 'Bearer {Token}'

item.description:
The Total Expert API uses OAuth2.0 to authorize and authenticate requests to the API.

Before you can use the API, you must first obtain an access token by using the ‘/token’ POST endpoint. Please obtain the token by supplying your client credentials (highlighted above) or an authorization code. Once you have your token, you will use it in the Authorization header of subsequent requests.

  • Total Expert maintains all production and sandbox/test environments behind the same URL. Your organization will be provided with separate credentials for the production and sandbox/test environments.
  • The Authentication token is good for 3600 seconds (60 mins).
  • You will retrieve a token for the highest level of scopes you need for the subsequent calls. Highly recommended best practice is to retrieve the token and cache it for the full hour that it’s valid then request a new token towards the end of the hour.
  • The Total Expert API has a limit of 1,000 requests per minute on all endpoints.
  • It might be necessary to requeue the requests for certain response codes. Ensure your organization has a process for error handling. See ‘Return Codes’ section above.

item.description:
Endpoints for interacting with the contacts resource.

Attributes
Field Assignable Type Description
id No numeric Generated identifier for contact.
address Yes string Street address portion of contact's address.
address_2 Yes string Line 2 portion of contact's address.
birthday Yes string Contact's birthday, formatted as a date with 1970 as the year. Preferred format: '1970-MM-DD'
city Yes string City portion of contact's address.
close_date Yes string Date/time contact closed. Preferred format: 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss'
creation_date Yes string Date of creation of this contact. Preferred format: 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss'
credit_score Yes string TE credit rating of contact. Accepted values: 'Excellent', 'Good', 'Fair', 'Poor', 'Very Poor'
credit_score_date Yes string Date/time of contact's credit score. Preferred format: 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss'
email Yes string Contact's personal email address.
email_work Yes string Contact's work email address.
employer_address Yes string Street address portion of contact's employer's address.
employer_address_2 Yes string Line 2 portion of contact's employer's address.
employer_city Yes string City portion of contact's employer's address.
employer_license_number Yes string Contact's employer's license number.
employer_name Yes string Name of contact's employer.
employer_state Yes string State portion of contact's employer's address.
employer_zip Yes string Zip code portion of contact's employer's address.
external_id Yes string Contact's external identifier, e.g. the unique identifier from the contact's source.
fax Yes string Contact's fax number. Preferred format: '(555)555-1234'
first_name Yes string Contact's first name.
internal_created_at No string Date of creation of this contact in TE systems. Format: 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss'
internal_updated_at No string Date of last change for this contact in TE systems. Format: 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss'

Deduplication Logic

Through the API, the external IDs array contains a contact’s unique identifier that comes from the external source. If there is a match within the external IDs array, the contact is successfully matched as well.

  • If the external IDs array does not contain a match, the logic looks for matches on first name, last name, and email.
  • If the first name, last name, and email do not match, the logic looks for matches on first name, last name, and address, city, state, and zip code.
  • If the first name, last name, address, city, stat, and zip code does not match, the logic looks for matches on first name, last name, and home phone.
  • If the first name, last name, and home phone does not match, the logic looks for matches on first name, last name, and cell phone.
  • If the first name, last name, and cell phone does not match, the logic looks for matches on first name, last name, and office phone.
  • If the first name, last name, and home phone does not match, the system will create a new contact.

item.description:
Endpoints for interacting with the contact surveys resource.

Overview

Surveys are a flexible data structure that allow integrations to store additional details around a contact that aren’t supported by the standard contact field set. For example, if a contact was interested in a refinance opportunity and supplied information about their property location, value, and existing mortgage, etc., you could store this information in a survey response and tie it to that contact.

Advantages of using the surveys endpoint

There are a few advantages to using the surveys endpoint:

  • Multiple survey structures can be created for an organization for different purposes. You can have one for refinance, auto loan interest, or any other data you wish to collect from your contacts.
  • A contact can submit multiple surveys and new submissions will show up in the survey response area in the UI rather than overwriting old data. This makes it easy to keep track of different interactions with the contact.
  • Contact survey responses can be used to trigger marketing automation and can also be used as different conditions within the journey.
General Flow

To submit survey responses to the API (examples in the Contact Survey Responses documentation), you first need to create the survey. The survey is structured as a set of questions and potential answers with their field types.

When creating the survey via the API, the API will return a survey ID in its response. Once you have that ID, you can retrieve the IDs of the questions from the API for use when creating a survey response.

Now that you have the IDs of the questions, you can create survey responses for that specific organization when data is being sent to Total Expert from your platform as described in the Contact Surveys Response documentation.

Note
If you are sending standard contact data with a survey, that will have to be sent first in a separate request so that you can obtain the Total Expert contact ID that you want to associate the survey with.

item.description:
The communication consent toolset provides a mechanism for recording the consent records your organization collects from your contacts. This tool is currently tailored specifically for telephone communication by an agentic A.I. application.

The API is designed around 2 primary operations: "Consent Grant" and "Consent Revoke". In order for consent to be revoked, it must have been previously granted.

Once consent has been granted, the corresponding Journey Condition will allow or block the AI Sales Assistant from making automated calls depending on the status of the Contact's AI Consent. AI Consent status will also be displayed on the Contact Profile, with an option to revoke manually through the User Interface.

The consent api follows the same command structure that the other Contact API endpoints for identifiying your contact, plus an object that describes your "grant" or revocation "revoke".

Note: Consent grant may be attached for a Create Contact (POST) or a Update Contact (PATCH). Revoking consent must be performed as a Contact Update (PATCH).

Parameters

first_name string true refer to Consent Create and update for the full list of contact parameters.

email string: A valid email false ...
grant_consent or revoke_consent Object true

.communication_channel string true "phone"

The following endpoints are in limited availability and are not recommended for general use. For questions about these endpoints, please reach out to support.

The varying contact endpoints that are associated with the following collections are used for

  • Adding contacts

  • Updating existing contacts

  • Transferring ownership of contacts

  • Obtaining the TE ID of contacts

  • Creating and submitting Contact Surveys

  • Creating contact groups, etc.

Tips for using the Contact endpoints

  • You will see a “duplicate” response if utilizing the Create (POST) method for updating existing contacts. However, the original entity will be updated.

  • You may want to utilize more than one identifier, such as ‘email address,’ if your organization has overlap when specifying the owner of a contact based on the User’s External ID.

  • If the data field does not exist within your environment, it is better to not submit this attribute in the request – rather than submitting it as blank. Ex: Do not submit a date of “0000-00-00”

  • Only use valid dates when submitting through the API. Omit the attribute if the date does not exist.

  • The maximum number of contacts returned per page on a GET request is 100. Specify using ‘?page[size]=100’

Why Contacts Are Important

Ensuring that you have the most up-to-date contact information within your TE system allows you to confidently send relevant communication, enable the right kinds of marketing automation at the right time, strengthen both your new and past relationships with customers and increase your overall brand image.

Contact Source

If the contact is coming from a third-party lead generating source, such as LeadPops, Velocify, LendingTree, etc. it is recommended to call use the source attribute in the call.

Contact Ownership

Specifying the owner of a contact is important because they are the only user that has the ability to remove or share/assign the contact record to other users within the TE system.

As an admin that is POSTing contacts to the TE system, you need to specify the contact’s owner. When specifying who the contact owner is, you can use the following settable fields within the request:

  • Username

  • ID

  • External ID

  • Email
    You do not need to specify the contact’s owner if you have user-level authentication access.

How to Change Contact Ownership

Similar to specifying the contact’s owner, you need to have admin-level authentication access. A POST call is required to update the owner of an already created contact. Simply include the contact ID and the updated owner ID in call. Deduplication logic will apply (see below for details).

Contact Webhooks

Total Expert has webhooks for the following contact interactions:

  • Contact Update

  • Contact Creation

  • Contact Archived

Check out the Webhook documentation for more details on how to subscribe to these webhooks.

item.description:
Important Note: As part of Total Expert’s new Lead Management feature, this new endpoint has been created. Because both the new endpoint (v1/lead-opportunities) and the existing (v1/leads) endpoint deal with “leads” in the platform, there is a conflict with the nomenclature used by both endpoints.

This section of the documentation refers exclusively to the new v1/lead-opportunities endpoint.

For information on the older v1/leads endpoint, formerly called Lead Opportunities in the documentation, please see the “ALM Leads (formerly Lead Opportunities)” section.

Unless and until further notice, users cannot utilize both endpoints concurrently.

The Lead Opportunities endpoints allow lead providers to POST, GET, and PATCH lead and lead opportunity details, including offer details and custom fields.

Base Endpoint: /v1/lead-opportunities
OAuth Scope: leadOpportunitiesSalesPipelineInteraction

Supported Operations

  • GET /v1/lead-opportunities - List with pagination, filtering, and sorting

  • GET /v1/lead-opportunities/{id} - Get specific lead opportunity

  • POST /v1/lead-opportunities - Create new lead opportunity

  • PATCH /v1/lead-opportunities/{id} - Update existing lead opportunity

Pagination

All list endpoints support pagination:

  • page[number] - Page number (default: 1, min: 1)

  • page[size] - Items per page (default: 25, min: 1)

Response includes pagination links:

{
  "items": [...],
  "links": {"first": 1, "last": 10, "next": 2, "prev": null}
}

Filtering

Use comma-separated field=value expressions:

filter=contact_id=123,user_id=456

Supported Filter Fields:

  • contact_id - Filter by contact ID

  • user_id - Filter by user ID

Sorting

Use sort query parameter with optional - prefix for descending:

sort=created_at        # Ascending
sort=-updated_at       # Descending

Allowed Sort Fields:

  • created_at - Creation date

  • updated_at - Last update date

  • lead_stage - Lead stage

  • loan_purpose - Loan purpose

Behavior:

  • Uses first field only if multiple provided

  • Case-insensitive, whitespace trimmed

  • Invalid field returns 400 error

Required Fields for Creation

Must provide ONE of these combinations:

  1. first_name, last_name, source, phone

  2. first_name, last_name, source, email

Product Validation

  • product.type and product.values must be provided together

  • product.values.loan_purpose is required when product is provided

  • Partial updates merge new values with existing product values

Update Requirements

  • contact_id is always required for PATCH requests

  • Updates target three independent areas:

    1. Assignment (assigned_user)

      1. user_id

      2. email

Example:

  "assigned_user": {
    "user_id": 789
  },

or

  "assigned_user": {
    "email": "john@example.com"
  },

  • Stage (stage.id)

  • Lead Opportunity data (other fields)

  • Partial failures return both successes and errors

Error Response Codes

  • 400 - Bad request (invalid body, missing fields, invalid filter/sort)

  • 404 - Not found (lead opportunity doesn't exist)

  • 422 - Unprocessable entity (page number out of range)

  • 500 - Internal server error

Valid Attributes

With the Total Expert Insights API, you can provide insights from events occurring within your platform which can be leveraged to drive marketing automation in Total Expert. To begin using insights through the API, you will need to coordinate with our team to create new insight types specific to your integration. Once these insight types are created, they can be used to create insights associated with any contact within TE (that you have access to).

item.description:
Endpoints for interacting with the users resource. These endpoints are restricted to organization admin users.

Attributes

Field Assignable Type Description
id No numeric Generated identifier for user.
email Yes* string User's email address. *Cannot be modified after initial assignment.
external_id Yes string User's external identifier.
info Yes object Collection of user details. See the "User Information Attributes" table for available attributes.
internal_created_at No string Date of creation of this user in TE systems. Format: 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss'
internal_updated_at No string Date of last change for this user in TE systems. Format: 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss'
last_login_date No string Date this user last logged into the TE system. Format: 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss'
licenses Yes Array of objects Collection of state user licenses. See the "User Licenses Attributes" table for available attributes.
disclaimers Yes Array of objects Collection of disclaimers. See the "User Disclaimers Attributes" table for available attributes.
settings_marketing Yes object Collection of user marketing settings. See the "User Marketing Settings Attributes" table for available attributes.
status Yes integer 0 - User is inactive. 1 - User is active. On user creation, if this is not provided, an active user is created.
type Yes string One of: "Realtor", "Lender", "Title"
username No string User's TE username. Read only. On user creation, this is generated from the user's email. For example, an email of "John.Smith@totalexpert.com" would create a username like "john-smith-totalexpert####", where none or up to four digits may be appended.
saml_subject_id No string Custom subject ID for this user for SSO.

User Information Attributes

Field Assignable Type Description
address Yes string Street address portion of user's address.
address_2 Yes string Line 2 portion of user's address.
city Yes string City portion of user's address.
state Yes string State portion of user's address.
zip_code Yes string Zip code portion of user's address.
first_name Yes string User's first name.
last_name Yes string User's last name.
phone_cell Yes string User's cell phone number, preferred format: '(555)555-1234'
phone_office Yes string User's office phone number, preferred format: '(555)555-1234'
phone_fax Yes string User's fax number, preferred format: '(555)555-1234'
job_title Yes string User's job title
cost_center Yes string Value used for accounting purposes. Typically used by an organization to determine how a user is segmented for billing within the organization.
website Yes string The user's homepage.
testimonial_url Yes string Link to page (usually from user's website) that features testimonials about working with that user
timezone_name Yes string The time zone the user operates in.
location_id Yes string
company Yes string Employer of user

User Marketing Settings Attributes

Field Assignable Type Description
agent_bio Yes string User's professional bio
application_url Yes string Link to Loan Officer's page where a contact can start a loan application
daily_spend_threshold Yes float Dollar amount user is authorized to spend of their organization cost share per day
disclaimer Yes string User's disclaimer text.
icon_one_img_url Yes string Link to image (1) to import for use in specific marketing material.
icon_two_img_url Yes string Link to image (2) to import for use in specific marketing material.
icon_three_img_url Yes string Link to image (3) to import for use in specific marketing material.
license_title Yes string User's license title.
logo_img_url Yes string Link to image to import as the user's logo image.
profile_img_url Yes string Link to image to import as the user's TE profile image.
short_name Yes string User's short name which can be used for links in their email signatures
social_facebook Yes string Link to personal or business page for the user on Facebook
social_google Yes string Link to personal or business page for the user on Google
social_linkedin Yes string Link to personal or business page for the user on LinkedIn
social_twitter Yes string Link to personal or business page for the user on Twitter
user_quote Yes string Secondary mission statement for the user. Used on specific marketing material.
weekly_spend_threshold Yes float Dollar amount user is authorized to spend of their organization cost share per week
wistia_id Yes string User's Wistia.com video identifier
post_close_survey_url Yes string url for the user's post close survey

Acceptable formats for images (any of the *_img_url fields) are: jpeg, jpg, png, and gif. The domains which host the image URLs must be pre-registered with Total Expert.

User Disclaimer Attributes

Field Assignable Type Description
disclaimer_name Yes string Name of the disclaimer.
content Yes string Content of the disclaimer.
type Yes object Type of the disclaimer. Please see "User Disclaimer Type Attributes" table for available attributes.

User Disclaimer Type Attributes

Field Assignable Type Description
name Yes string Type of the disclaimer. The available types are 'Print Disclaimer', 'Web Disclaimer', 'Email Disclaimer', 'License Number', and 'Sub-Disclaimer'

User License Attributes

Field Assignable Type Description
license_name Yes string Name of license. For example, a U.S. state abbreviation.
content Yes string Content of license. For example, the license number.

Uniqueness

Option Fields
1 username
2 email
3 external_id

Relationships

Relationship Assignable Type Settable Fields Description
expenditure_approver Yes User username, id, external_id, email User responsible for approving overages on daily or weekly organization cost share threshold.
role Yes User Role id, role_name Role of the user.
teams Yes Team id, team_name Teams to add this user to. Array of Team objects.

Use a team's "managers" and "remove_managers" relationships to define the users managing a team. Alternatively, use the Teams endpoints to assign or remove team managers.

Special POST/PATCH Attributes

These attributes are used to manipulate the user but are neither user attributes or relationships. These attributes will not appear in responses.

Field Type Settable Fields Description
remove_teams Team team_name, id Teams to remove this user from. Array of team objects.
remove_licenses License license_name Licenses to remove from this user. Array of license objects.
remove_disclaimers Disclaimer disclaimer_name, type Disclaimers to remove from this user. Array of disclaimer objects.

Filtering

Use the 'filter=attribute_name=x,attribute_name_2=y' query to return the list of users that meet the filter criteria. For example, to filter users modified between Oct. 14, 2017 17:41:01 (UTC) and Oct. 15, 2017 17:41:09 (UTC), the following query could be used:

/users?filter=internal_updated_at_start=2017-10-14T17:41:01Z,internal_updated_at_end=2017-10-15T17:41:09Z

The supported filter attributes are shown in the following table.

Field Description
internal_updated_at_start ISO-8601 formatted date. The start of the time range of interest, inclusive.
internal_updated_at_end ISO-8601 formatted date. The end of the time range of interest, inclusive.
email User's email address.
username User's TE username.
status Indicator of user's status.
external_id User's external identifier.

Endpoints for interacting with the entities resource. These endpoints are restricted to organization admin users.

Attributes
Field Assignable Type Description
id No string Generated identifier for entity.
address Yes string Street address portion of entity's address.
address_2 Yes string Line 2 portion of entity's address.
city Yes string City portion of entity's address.
entity_name Yes string Name of the entity.
external_id Yes string entity's external identifier, e.g. the unique identifier from the entity's source.
state Yes string State portion of entity's address.
zip_code Yes string Zip code portion of entity's address.
phone Yes string Entity's phone number, preferred format: '(555)555-1234'
internal_created_at No string Date of creation of this entity in TE systems. Format: 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss'
internal_updated_at No string Date of last change for this entity in TE systems. Format: 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss'

Relationships

The "owner" section at the top level of the POST, PATCH, or DELETE is required when contacts are included in the request. All included contacts are created or updated for that owner, and only one owner can be used per request.

Some relationship types are discrete and can only have one child.

Relationship Assignable Type Settable Fields Description
owner Yes* User username, id, external_id, email Owning user of the entity. One to many relationship, so returned as an object. *Only assignable/visible if authenticated as an organization admin.
entity_type Yes Entity Type system_name Type for this entity. Many-to-one relationship, is returned as an object.
related_entities Yes * * *(See Related Entities Relationships Section, below)
custom Yes Custom Field *(See Custom Fields) *(See Custom Fields)

Related Entities Relationships

Relationship Assignable Type Settable Fields Description
relationship_type Yes Entity Relationship Type system_name The type of relationship to the target contacts.
children Yes Contacts * *(See contact documentation)

Special POST/PATCH Attributes - depending on posting endpoint

Relationship Assignable Type Settable Fields Description
children Yes Contacts * *(See contact documentation) - available when posting inside an entity
parent Yes Entity * *(See entity resource documentation, above) - Only available when posting inside a contact

Special POST/PATCH Attributes

These attributes are used to manipulate the entity but are neither entity attributes or relationships. These attributes will not appear in responses.

Field Type Settable Fields Description
remove_related_entities * * *(See Related Entities Relationships Section, above, to dissociate related entities)

Sorting

Use the 'sort=attribute_name,attribute_name_2' query to return the list of entities sorted by the given attribute. Use a minus sign in front of the attribute name to sort the results in descending order. For example, to sort by the internal_updated_at attribute and place the results in descending order, the URL would include:

/entities?sort=-internal_updated_at

The sort query supports the attributes listed in the Attributes table. The query does not support sorting by relationship values.

item.description:
Webhooks allow you to stay informed on certain events that occur within the platform. They serve as a mechanism that keeps the system in sync by allowing one application to deliver information to another application in real-time. In other words, you receive data immediately.

When Should I Subscribe to Webhooks?

A subscription to a webhook is useful if your organization has a mirrored copy of your TE database, and you want to be informed of any changes that are occurring. Once you have a webhook, you retrieve data about a possible change. At that time, you can make the decision to update your database or not.

Webhook Examples:
  • Organizations or vendors that have a CRM separate from the TE system could be informed of any contact or lead that is manually added through the TE system and not the CRM first.
  • When contacts are being updated directly within the TE system and not the CRM. This ensures the other system(s) stay in sync.
  • Deleting contacts or archiving contacts within TE ensures that the correct contacts are removed from the CRM database as well.
  • If contacts opt out of email communication within TE, the other CRM database can be updated to ensure communication does not reach them.
Requesting Webhooks

The following must be included during a webhook request:

  • A URL where notifications are sent. This must be HTTPS protected by a valid certification.
  • A list of actions to subscribe to. To get a full list of these actions, use the fetch webhooks endpoint.
  • A secret field that is included in any webhook notification sent by TE to the specified URL. This is used to authenticate that the process is not malicious.
    -- A randomly generated HEX string of 32 to 64 characters is suggested. A secret of up to 255 characters is supported.
    -- This secret can be rotated by performing a PATCH against the endpoint using the subscription ID you received when first creating the subscription.
Webhook Notification Limitations

NOTE:

  • Users only receive notifications when the contact record is associated with your organization.
  • Users do not receive notifications from contacts that are not associated with their organization. Co-marketers of organizational contacts also do not receive notifications.
What Happens When a Request Action Occurs?

TE generates a webhook notification. This consists of an HTTP POST request sent to the URL provided in the request.

Example Webhook Body
{ 
  "item":"<item>", 
  "action":"<action>", 
  "id":<id>, 
  "hashValue":"<hashValue>", 
  "secret":"<secret>" 
}

Attributes

Attributes Descriptions
item Name of the subscribed item, ex: ‘CONTACT’
action Name of the subscribed verb, ex: ‘CREATED’
id The database ID of the item
hashValue The value generated from the affected record. (See below for more information.)
secret Secret that has been specified
What is the Hash Value?

The purpose of a hash value is to allow the user to view if the update has actually been made to the contact or not. Hash values are HEX strings that represent the contents of the affected record.

The hash value does not change if the notification is triggered on the same contact record without any actual changes happening to that specific contact. So, if you receive multiple notifications from one contact record without the hash value being update, you can safely ignore the second, third, fourth, etc. notification.

I.e. If a user saves a contact record within the TE UI without actually adjusting any of the contact’s information.

It is important to compare the hash value only to the most recent notification received. If a contact record has been modified but then reverts to its previous state, the last notification’s hash value would match the one from before the changes.

Webhook Endpoints

Endpoints for registering for webhooks in the TE system.

All webhooks in the TE system subscribe to a set of 'actions'. An action comprises an 'entity' and a 'verb'. Subscribable actions can be fetched from the 'webhook-actions' endpoint.

Each organization can have several webhooks, and each webhook can be registered to multiple actions.

request.description:
Leads and Contacts

A POST request for a new lead wil also create a new contact record, but only if a matching contact is not found. A matching contact is one that meets this criteria:

  • Has a first name identical to the request first_name
  • Has a last name identical tp the request last_name
  • Has an e-mail address or phone number field identical to those in the request
  • If owner_id is not in the request, the contact meets the above matching criteria and is owned by the same organization
  • If an owner_id is in the request, the contact meets the above matching criteria and is owned by the exact same user ID

A successful response from will return the ID of the new lead, and the ID of either the new contact or the existing, matched contact:

{
    "contact_id": 144558,
    "lead_id": 144559
}

Required Fields

One of the following combinations:

  • first_name, last_name, source, email
  • first_name, last_name, source, address, city, state, zip
  • first_name, last_name, source, phone_home
  • first_name, last_name, source, phone_cell
  • first_name, last_name, source, phone_office

Optional fields:

  • owner_id
  • All lead_opportunity fields,
  • All lead_opportunity_offers fields
  • custom fields

Lead Attributes

Field Data Type Description
tile string The contact's honorific/title, e.g. "Doctor"
first_name string The contact's first name
last_name string The contact's last name
suffix string The contact's suffix, e.g. "Jr."
nickname string The contact's preferred name
owner_id integer The Total Expert user ID that owns the contact/lead
address string Street address portion of contact's current address.
address_2 string Line 2 portion of contact's current address.
city string City portion of contact's current address.
state string State portion of current contact's address. Preferred
format: Two character state abbreviation, e.g. 'CA'
zip_code string Zip code portion of contact's current address.
Preferred format: 5 digit postal code, e.g. '90210'
birthday string Contact's birthday, formatted as a date with 1970 as
the year. Preferred format: '1970-MM-DD'
creation_date string Date of creation of this contact. Preferred format:
'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss'
last_contacted_date string Date/time of last interaction with contact. Preferred
format: 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss'
email string Contact's personal email address.
email_work string Contact's work email address.
phone_cell string Contact's cell phone number, preferred format:
'(555)555-1234'
phone_home string Contact's home phone number, preferred format:
'(555)555-1234'
phone_office string Contact's office phone number, preferred format:
'(555)555-1234'
ok_to_call boolean Indicator whether it is OK to call this contact.
True or 1 - Yes
False or 0 -No
ok_to_email boolean Indicator whether it is OK to call this contact.
True or 1 - Yes
False or 0 -No
ok_to_mail boolean Indicator whether it is OK to call this contact.
True or 1 - Yes
False or 0 -No
referred_by string Name of person by whom this contact was referred.
source string Source of the contact.
credit_score string Total Expert credit rating of the lead.
Available values:
Excellent, Good, Fair, Poor, Very Poor.
credit_score_date string Date/time of contact's last received credit score.
Preferred format: 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss'

Opportunity Attributes

Field Data Type Description
property_value integer
property_county string County which the property to be financed is
located, e.g. Alameda
property_zip string Postal Code of the property to be financed, e.g.
90210
property_state string State which the property is located. Preferred
format is two character state abbreviation, e.g.
'CA'
property_msa string Metropolitan area which the property is located,
e.g. 'Greater Los Angeles'
loan_amount integer Estimated loan amount requested, e.g. 250000
loan_down_payment integer Estimated down payment requested, e.g. 100000
loan_cash_out integer Estimated additional cash out amount requested,
e.g. 10000
property_type string Type of property to be financed, e.g. 'Single
Family Dettached'
property_use string Occupancy of the property to be financed, e.g.
'Owner Occupied'
loan_request_type string Loan purpose, e.g. “Purchase’ or “Cash-out
Refinance’
lead_price string Amount charged by source to generate lead
tracking_number string Unique identifier assigned by the source for the
lead
annual_income decimal Annual income of the lead.
first_time_buyer boolean Indicator if lead is a first time home buyer. True or 1
= Is a First Time Home Buyer
has_agent boolean Indicator if lead is working with a real estate
agent. True or 1 = Is working with an Agent
is_military boolean Indicator if lead is active duty or a veteran. True or 1
= is active duty or a veteran
self_credit_rating string Estimated credit rating of contact. Preferred
values: 'Excellent', 'Good', 'Fair', 'Poor', 'Very
Poor'
bankruptcy boolean Indicator if lead has had bankruptcy. True or 1 = has had
bankruptcy
foreclosure boolean Indicator if lead has had foreclosure. True or 1 = has had
foreclosure
found_home boolean Indicator if lead has located the property they
intend to finance. True or 1 = They have located a
home.
property_purchase_price decimal Contracted purchase price of the property to be
financed, e.g. 350000
is_fha_eligible boolean Indicator if lead is eligible for FHA product. True or 1 = Is
eligible for FHA product.
is_va_loan boolean Indicator of the offer selected is VA eligible.
True or 1 = VA Offer
present_ltv decimal Current Loan To Value ratio of the property to be
financed. Rounded to the nearest thousandth, e.g.
71.123
proposed_ltv decimal Requested Loan To Value ratio of the property to
be financed. Rounded to the nearest thousandth,
e.g. 74.123
term string Requested or selected term of the offer, e.g. 30
year fixed
estimated_payment decimal Estimated payment of the selected offer, e.g.
1234.55
apr decimal Annual Percentage Rate of the selected offer.
Rounded to the nearest thousandth, e.g. 3.625
market_value decimal Market value of the property to be financed.
Rounded to the nearest thousandth, e.g.
350000.000
rate_offer decimal Note Rate of the selected offer. Rounded to the
nearest thousandth, e.g. 3.125

Offers Attributes

The following represents the attributes of one offer object. Offers can be passed in an array [ ].

Field Data Type Description
offer_id integer
offer_type string Amortization type of the offer, ex. Fixed
loan_program_name string Name of the loan program of the offer, ex. Conf 30 Yr
Fixed
loan_amount decimal Loan amount used to generate the offer, ex. 250000
interest_rate decimal Interest rate of the offer, ex. 3.750
term string Amortization term of the offer, ex. 30
points decimal Price of the offer, ex. 1
investor string Investor used to generate the offer, ex. Wells Fargo
lock_term integer Lock period used to generate the offer, ex. 45
monthly_payment decimal Monthly Principle and Interest payment of the offer
down_payment decimal Down payment used to generate the offer
apr decimal Annual Percentage Rate of the offer

Custom Field Attributes

The optional custom attribute, if specified, should contain one or more objects, each object representing one custom field name and its value. The custom fields should be wrapped in an array:

"custom": [
        {
            "field_name": "first_datetime", 
            "value": "07/21/2023 00:00:00"
        },
        {
            "field_name": "date", 
            "value": "10/30/2023"
        }
    ]

A custom field definition of type "contact" that matches the given field_name must already exist for the POST to succeed. A POST request will not create new, adhoc custom field definitions.

Attributes of a custom field

Field Data Type Description
field_name string The system name of the custom field.
value variable, according to definition A custom value matching the data type of the custom field definition.

Data Types

The PATCH is sensitive to data types, and will error if types do not align with the types in the request body below.

If the value of a given attribute does not match the type specified in PATCH validation, the request should fail and tell you why.

Accepted type details:

  • Integer values, real, positive values only
  • String values must be wrapped in double quotation marks, as in "hello there"
  • Decimals can be decimal values or integer values
  • Booleans must be true, false, 0, or 1. Strings 'true' and 'false' are NOT accepted.

Updating Lead Stage

lead_stage can be updated with an integer, 1 through 5, represneting the following lifecycle stages of a lead:

  1. New Lead
  2. Contacted
  3. Application
  4. In Process
  5. Closed

Other values can be updated concurrently with lead_stage.

Updating Lead Opportunity Offers

offers can also be updated, but for each desired offer update, the offer_id of the given offer must be included, along with at least one other offer attribute

Important Note: As part of Total Expert’s new Lead Management feature, a new endpoint has been created. Because both the new endpoint (v1/lead-opportunities) and this existing (v1/leads) endpoint deal with “leads” in the platform, there is a conflict with the nomenclature used by both endpoints.

This section of the documentation refers exclusively to the existing, older v1/leads endpoint designed for Advanced Lead Management (ALM).

For information on the new v1/lead-opportunities endpoint, please see the “Lead Opportunities (New)” section.

No functional changes were made to the endpoint.

Unless and until further notice, users cannot utilize both endpoints concurrently.

The Lead Opportunities endpoints allow lead providers to POST, GET, and PATCH lead and lead opportunity details, including offer details and custom fields.

Authentication and Authorization

There are two means of authenticating for Lead Opportunity endpoints.

  1. The first is the typical bearer authentication flow, documented under the "Authentication" header above.

  2. Alternatively, the Lead Opportunities endpoints support "Simple Auth," which can be enabled by Total Expert. "Simple Auth" supports authentication via an api_key attribute/value within request bodies, or else sending a header of api-key. Note the underscore and hypen differentiation, which is by design.

Relationships

Relationship Assignable Type Settable Fields Description
owner Yes* User username, id, external_id, email Owning user of the lead. One to many relationship, so returned as an object. *Only available on POST - changing owner on patch is not currently supported

Note: the use of the owner_id property is still supported, but deprecated in favor of this relationship.

Both means of authentication require the credentials to contain the leadOpportunityInteraction scope.

Optional: The _getUsers_ scope is required to retrieve unique user IDs from the _v1/users_ endpoint. User IDs are used to as _owner_id_ in _POST_ requests, should the request sender desire to assign a lead directly to a user.

request.description:
Retrieves archived email content using the encoded messageId format: id-{organizationId}-{messageId}.

The organization ID embedded in the messageId is validated against the authenticated caller's organization. A mismatch returns 404 — not 403 — to avoid leaking whether a message exists.

Path parameter: id-{orgId}-{msgId} — replace 42 with the org ID and 9001 with the message ID.

Required filter: user_id={userId} — the user must belong to the caller's org.

description.content: Required. Comma-separated key=value pairs. Must include user_id. The user must belong to the caller's organization.

request.description:
Retrieves archived email content using a plain numeric messageId.

The organization is inferred from the authenticated caller's token — no org ID is embedded in the messageId. The caller's org is validated against the message sender's org inside the DataManager.

Path parameter: plain integer string — replace 9001 with the message ID.

Required filter: user_id={userId} — the user must belong to the caller's org.

description.content: Required. Comma-separated key=value pairs. Must include user_id. The user must belong to the caller's organization.

item.description:
Endpoints for retrieving archived email content.

All requests require an OAuth2 Bearer token with the emailInteraction scope.

messageId Formats

Two formats are accepted for the {messageId} path parameter:

Format Example Description
id-{organizationId}-{messageId} id-42-9001 Encoded. Org ID must match caller's org or a 404 is returned.
{messageId} 9001 Raw numeric. Org is inferred from the caller's token.

Filter Parameter

The filter query parameter accepts comma-separated key=value pairs.

Required key: user_id — must be a TE user ID belonging to the caller's organization.

Example: filter=user_id=12345

Notes

  • Read-only endpoint — no POST, PATCH, or DELETE operations are supported.

  • content is raw HTML — render it in a sandboxed context to avoid XSS exposure.

  • 404 instead of 403 on org mismatch — when the org embedded in an encoded messageId does not match the caller's org, the API returns 404 (not 403) intentionally, to avoid leaking whether a message exists.

  • Raw numeric format has no early org check — for plain numeric messageId, the org is only validated inside the data layer by comparing the caller's org against the message sender's org fetched from the database. If they don't match, a 404 is returned.

  • user_id must be in the caller's org — the user_id passed in the filter is verified against the organization_users table before any message lookup occurs.

  • Caller must belong to an org — if the authenticated token has no associated organization, the request is rejected with 400.

Response Attributes

Field Type Description
items.file_name string The messageId value passed in the request, returned as-is.
items.content string The full HTML content of the archived email.
links.first numeric Always 1 — pagination anchor.
links.last numeric Always 1 — single result, no paging.
links.next null Always null — no next page.
links.prev null Always null — no previous page.

Error Responses

Status Trigger
400 Bad Request messageId is missing from the path.
400 Bad Request messageId is not a plain integer and does not match the id-{orgId}-{msgId} pattern.
400 Bad Request user_id is missing or non-numeric in the filter query parameter.
400 Bad Request Authenticated caller has no associated organization.
400 Bad Request user_id does not exist in the caller's organization.
400 Bad Request Email archive file is missing or empty in storage.
404 Not Found Encoded messageId contains an org ID that does not match the caller's org.
404 Not Found No message found for the given ID, or message belongs to a different org.
500 Internal Server Error Unexpected server-side failure retrieving the archive.

item.description:
Endpoints for rendering email templates with variable substitution.

All requests require an OAuth2 Bearer token with the emailInteraction scope.

Overview

Renders an email template (by template ID or inline HTML) with placeholders resolved for a given sender, recipient, and optional context (loan, account, comarketer, video, ODC push result).

Request Body Fields

Field Required Type Description
id Yes* numeric Template ID to render. Must be a positive integer. *Either id or content.html must be provided.
content.html Yes* string Inline HTML to render instead of a saved template. *Either id or content.html must be provided.
content.subject No string Custom subject line. If omitted, falls back to the saved template's subject.
sender_id Yes numeric TE user ID of the sender. Must belong to the caller's organization.
recipient No object Contact to resolve placeholders for. See Recipient Object below.
comarketer_id No numeric TE user ID of a comarketer. Must be a valid comarketer for the sender.
loan_id No numeric Loan ID to use for loan placeholder resolution. Must belong to the caller's org. Mutually exclusive with account_id.
account_id No numeric Account ID to use for product placeholder resolution. Must belong to the caller's org. Mutually exclusive with loan_id.
odc_push_result_id No numeric ODC push result ID for ODC placeholder resolution.
video No object Video metadata to inject into the template.

Recipient Object

Field Required Type Description
id No numeric TE lead/contact ID. Must be a positive integer and belong to the caller's org.

Response Attributes

Field Type Description
results[].recipient_id numeric null
results[].rendered_html string Fully rendered HTML with all placeholders substituted.
results[].rendered_subject string Fully rendered subject line. Empty string if no subject was provided.

Org Validation

  • sender_id must belong to the caller's organization.

  • loan_id (if provided) is validated via the loan officer's org.

  • account_id (if provided) is validated via the account manager's org.

  • recipient.id (if provided) is validated via the lead owner's org.

  • Template id (if provided) must belong to the caller's org.

Error Responses

Status Trigger
400 Bad Request Neither id nor content.html is provided.
400 Bad Request id is not a positive integer.
400 Bad Request sender_id is missing or not a positive integer.
400 Bad Request sender_id does not exist or does not belong to the caller's org.
400 Bad Request comarketer_id is not a positive integer, or is not a valid comarketer for the sender.
400 Bad Request loan_id is not a positive integer, or does not belong to the caller's org.
400 Bad Request account_id is not a positive integer, or does not belong to the caller's org.
400 Bad Request Both loan_id and account_id are provided (mutually exclusive).
400 Bad Request recipient is not an object, or recipient.id is missing or not a positive integer.
400 Bad Request recipient.id does not belong to the caller's org.
403 Forbidden Authenticated user has no user ID or organization context.
404 Not Found Template id not found for the sender, or belongs to a different org.
500 Internal Server Error Template render failed unexpectedly.

Notes

  • id and content.html are mutually inclusive of at least one — if id is given, the saved template's HTML and subject are used as the base; content.html and content.subject override them if also provided.

  • loan_id and account_id are mutually exclusive — providing both returns a 400.

  • Recipient resolves contact placeholders — if recipient.id is provided, placeholders for contact, journey contact, and opportunity offers are all populated.

  • Template org check uses org_id on the email record — not just the sender relationship.

request.description:
Uploads a user image as raw binary in the request body.

The image is stored in S3 under the target user's marketing images path and a record is created in the database.

Headers required:

  • Content-Type — MIME type of the image (image/jpeg, image/png, image/gif)

item.description:
Endpoints for uploading user images.

All requests require an OAuth2 Bearer token with the emailInteraction scope.

Request Format

The image is sent as raw binary in the request body. The Content-Type header determines the image format.

Allowed Content Types

Content-Type Extension
image/jpeg .jpg
image/png .png
image/gif .gif

Headers

Header Required Description
Authorization Yes Bearer token with emailInteraction scope.
Content-Type Yes MIME type of the image. Must be image/jpeg, image/png, or image/gif.
X-User-Id Yes TE user ID of the user to upload the image for. Must be an integer. Must belong to the same organization as the caller.

Org Validation

The caller and the target user (X-User-Id) must belong to the same organization. If they differ, a 404 is returned.

File Constraints

  • Maximum file size: 5 MB

  • MIME type must match the Content-Type header — mismatches are rejected with 422.

Response Attributes

Field Type Description
id numeric Generated identifier for the uploaded image record.
user_id numeric TE user ID the image belongs to.
url string Public URL to access the uploaded image.
filename string Generated filename used to store the image.
created_on string Timestamp of upload. Format: YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss.

Error Responses

Status Trigger
400 Bad Request Content-Type header is missing or not one of the allowed types.
400 Bad Request X-User-Id header is missing.
400 Bad Request X-User-Id is not a valid integer.
400 Bad Request Request body is empty.
400 Bad Request File size exceeds 5 MB.
404 Not Found Target user does not exist or is inactive.
404 Not Found Target user belongs to a different organization than the caller.
422 Unprocessable Entity MIME type of the uploaded file does not match the Content-Type header.
500 Internal Server Error Upload to S3 failed.
500 Internal Server Error Database record creation failed after successful upload.

Notes

  • Binary body only — the image must be sent as raw bytes in the request body, not as multipart/form-data.

  • 404 on org mismatch — a 404 (not 403) is returned when the target user belongs to a different org, to avoid leaking user existence.

  • Filename is auto-generated — the original filename is not used; a random filename is generated server-side.

  • Image is stored in S3 — the returned url is a public link to the uploaded file under the user's marketing images path.
